attribution.note: Marcus directly asserts the bankruptcy filing in his own prose.

semantics.note: The normalisation faithfully extracts the bankruptcy assertion without adding shutdown or liquidation.

contract.note: Treating the brand as its operating company and requiring a petition by publication is an ordinary reading.

evidence.note: The October 12 company disclosure confirms its Chapter 11 process before publication; it is not an independent finding.
The October 13 U.S. Trustee notice identifies the debtor and case and independently confirms that a voluntary petition had been filed.

reviews.rationale: The company announcement and official Trustee notice establish a bankruptcy petition before October 14. Continued platform operation does not contradict a Chapter 11 filing. No material counterevidence is supplied.

attribution.note: Marcus adopts the bond figure in his own prose, alongside the embedded market commentary.

semantics.note: The normalisation preserves the firm numerical observation and the explicitly tentative market interpretation.

contract.note: Approximately 15% secondary-market yield on at least one issue, including an intraday high, is a fair ordinary reading. The hedged market interpretation is appropriately excluded from scoring.

evidence.note: Contemporaneous reporting identifies the 2032 issue and an October 13 intraday yield of 15%. It relies on an investor's chart rather than independently retrieved trades.
The reported October 13 yield of 14.7% on identified 2031 notes rounds to 15%. Its attributed TRACE data were not independently retrieved.

reviews.rationale: The packet supports the firm yield observation through contemporaneous reporting and corroborating secondary data. A lower closing yield does not refute an intraday high. Underlying trades remain unverified. The hedged inference about credit markets is not adjudicated.
